All 14 queries ran and gave plausible answers. I checked T12 and T13 by hand against `orders.csv`, and T1 against `users.json`. The rest I only checked by reading the output. A few of them use slightly odd forms, because `qlang` rejected my first attempts:

- T6 writes the sort key as `~([…])`. The harness refused a bare `~[…]`.
- T3 and T10 give maps with string keys (T10's raw output prints them as keywords).
- T14 gave `elderberry-banana-cherry-apple-date-kiwi-fig`.

T1: /data/users | filter ~(/active | eq true) | filter ~(at :email | coalesce "" | lower | endsWith "@example.com") | count
T2: /data/users | filter ~(/roles | any ~(lower | eq "admin")) | sort ~(/name | lower) | * /name
T3: /data/users | groupBy ~(at :profile | at :country | coalesce "unknown") * count
T4: /data/users * (at :profile | at :age) | filter ~(ne null) | avg | round 2
T5: filter ~(/state | eq "open") * /labels | flat | * (/name | lower) | distinct | sort
T6: sort ~([(/comments | desc) /number]) | take 3 * {:number /number :assignee (at :assignee | at :login)}
T7: filter ~(/state | eq "open") | filter ~(at :assignee | ne null) | groupBy ~(/assignee/login) * count
T8: unionOf /dependencies /devDependencies | entries | filter ~(/1 | startsWith "^") | sort ~(/0) * ([(/0 | keyword) /1] | join "@")
T9: /services | filter ~(at :enabled | eq true) | filter ~(/port | gt 8000) | * (/name | lower) | sort | join ","
T10: lines | filter ~(split " " | /1 | eq "ERROR") | groupBy ~(split " " | /2) * count
T11: lines | filter ~(contains "ms=") | * (split " " | filter ~(startsWith "ms=") | first | drop 3 | parseJson) | avg | round 1
T12: lines | drop 1 | filter ~(ne "") * split "," | filter ~(/5 | lower | eq "shipped") | filter ~(/4 | ne "") | * mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson) | sum | round 2
T13: lines | drop 1 | filter ~(ne "") * split "," | filter ~(/5 | lower | ne "cancelled") | filter ~(/4 | ne "") | groupBy ~(/1) * (* mulOf (/3 | parseJson) (/4 | parseJson) | sum | round 2) | entries * {:customer (/0 | keyword) :total /1} | sort ~(/total | desc) | take 2
T14: ["Banana" "apple" "Cherry" "banana" "fig" "APPLE" "date" "kiwi" "Fig" "elderberry"] * lower | distinct | sort ~([(count | desc) /]) | join "-"
